lesson.subject: data-ai
lesson.title: Using AI Helpers Safely
lesson.summary: Use voice and picture helpers with a grown-up, check what they say and keep private things private.
learning_objectives: Say what an AI helper can and cannot do
Ask a trusted adult to check answers

standards.text: Societal impact: AI can impact the world in positive and negative ways
Use technology safely and respectfully, keeping personal information private; identify where to go for help

success_criteria: I can say what an AI helper is
I can keep private things private
I know to check answers and tell a trusted adult
lesson.real_life: Asking a voice helper for prayer times or the date of Eid, then checking with family.

warm_up.hint: It notices light, sound or movement.

blocks.markdown: Today's big question: how do we use AI helpers safely?
blocks.say: Today we meet AI helpers. Sam wants to ask his family's voice helper a question.

blocks.alt: A thin crescent moon in a dark purple evening sky with tree branches
blocks.caption: A thin crescent moon. People watch for it to mark a new month.
blocks.credit: Photo by Rob Wicks on Unsplash
blocks.say: Sam wants to know the day of Eid. The new crescent moon helps people decide.

blocks.markdown: An **AI helper** is a program that can talk or answer questions.
blocks.say: A voice helper listens and answers. It uses AI, which is a computer program made by people.

scenes.caption: Listen.
scenes.say: Sam asks a question. The helper listens with a microphone.

scenes.caption: Find.
scenes.say: The program finds an answer from lots of information.

scenes.caption: Answer.
scenes.say: It speaks the answer. It sounds clever. But it is only a program.

question.explanation: A voice helper is a program made by people.

options.text: A program that listens and answers

blocks.markdown: A helper can be **wrong**. Check important answers.
blocks.say: A helper sounds sure. But it can be wrong. Sam asks when Eid falls. It says it is unsure.

scenes.caption: Not sure.
scenes.say: Sam asks: what day is Eid? The helper says, I am not sure.

scenes.caption: The moon.
scenes.say: Eid depends on the moon. A helper might not know the latest news.

scenes.caption: Check.
scenes.say: So Sam checks with Abbu and the calendar. That is wise.

question.prompt: An AI helper is always right.
question.explanation: A helper can be wrong or unsure.

blocks.title: Sam asks about Eid
blocks.transcript: Sam wants to know the day of Eid. He asks the voice helper. The helper says it is not sure. Eid depends on the moon. So Sam asks Abbu. Abbu listens carefully. They check the calendar and the news about the moon. Sam never tells the helper his address. That is private. Sam sees a picture of a cow with five legs. It looks odd. He tells Abbu. Abbu says, good checking, Sam. At home they put up their three AI rules.
blocks.caption: Sam asks a voice helper when Eid falls and checks with Abbu.

blocks.markdown: Ask safe questions with a **grown-up** beside you.
blocks.say: Sam asks with Abbu beside him. A safe question is about facts, like how far away the Moon is.

scenes.caption: Safe.
scenes.say: A safe question: how many days are in a week?

scenes.caption: Unsafe.
scenes.say: An unsafe thing to say: our home address or a password.

scenes.caption: Private.
scenes.say: Keep private things private, even when it feels friendly.

blocks.title: Sort the questions
blocks.goal: Move the 6 questions into Safe or Not safe.

question.prompt: Which is a safe thing to ask a helper?
question.explanation: A fact question keeps private things private.

options.text: How many legs does a spider have?

blocks.text: Stop 2: Check with a book or adult

blocks.markdown: **Check** an answer with a book or a trusted adult.
blocks.say: After the helper answers, Sam checks. He looks in a book. He asks Abbu.

blocks.alt: An open book with its pages fanned out against a plain background
blocks.caption: Checking in a book is a good way to be sure.
blocks.credit: Photo by Olga Tutunaru on Unsplash
blocks.say: A book is one way to check. A grown-up can help too.

scenes.caption: The answer.
scenes.say: The helper says: a spider has eight legs.

scenes.caption: Book.
scenes.say: Sam checks in a book. It says eight legs too.

scenes.caption: Sure.
scenes.say: Now Sam is sure. Checking helps us trust good answers.

blocks.title: Ask and check
materials: A voice helper or app, with a grown-up
instructions: Ask a safe question together, like how many days are in a week.
Look up the answer in a book too.
Did they match? Tell a grown-up.
blocks.say: Now you try. Ask a grown-up to help you ask and check.

question.prompt: It is a good idea to check important answers.

points: Ask safe questions with a grown-up
Check answers in a book or with an adult
blocks.say: Let us remember. Ask safe questions with a grown-up. Check the answers.

blocks.markdown: A picture can look **real** and still be made up.
blocks.say: A picture can look real but be made up. A computer can make pictures that never happened.

scenes.caption: Odd clue.
scenes.say: This picture shows a cow with five legs. That is odd.

scenes.caption: Check the facts.
scenes.say: Cows have four legs. The picture may be made up.

scenes.caption: Ask.
scenes.say: We ask a grown-up if we are not sure.

question.prompt: A picture shows a cow with five legs. What could that mean?
question.explanation: Odd details can show a picture is made up.

options.text: The picture may be made up

blocks.markdown: Some people **trick** others online. Ask a grown-up.
blocks.say: Some people make fake pictures to trick us. They may want us to click, or to believe something that is not true.

blocks.markdown: Play the memory game. Then spot a picture that cannot be real.
blocks.say: First a memory game. Then spot the odd one that cannot be real.

blocks.markdown: A family can write **rules** for AI helpers.
blocks.say: Sam's family writes AI rules. A rule keeps everyone safe. They write three.
Rule one: ask a grown-up before using a helper.
Rule two: never share private things like our name, address or password.

scenes.caption: Rule 1.
scenes.say: Rule one is a hand up. Ask a grown-up first.

scenes.caption: Rule 2.
scenes.say: Rule two is a padlock. Keep private things private.

scenes.caption: Rule 3.
scenes.say: Rule three is a magnifier. Check important answers.

blocks.title: Our family rules
instructions: Write three rules for using AI helpers.
Draw a picture for each rule.
Put your rules where everyone can see them.
blocks.say: Rule three: check important answers. Tell a grown-up if something worries us.

question.prompt: Match each rule to its reason.
question.hint: Why do we have each rule?
question.explanation: Each rule has a good reason.

blocks.say: If something online scares or confuses us, we stop and tell a trusted adult. We are not in trouble.

scenes.caption: Worried.
scenes.say: A message on the screen makes Sam feel worried.

scenes.caption: Stop.
scenes.say: He puts the device down and finds Abbu.

scenes.caption: Tell.
scenes.say: Abbu listens and helps. Telling was the right thing.
